2027-03-19.title: St Joseph, Spouse of the Blessed Virgin Mary
readings: The Lord God will give him the throne of his ancestor David
His dynasty shall last for ever
Joseph did as the angel of the Lord commanded him
2027-03-19.alt: Solemnity. The readings of Friday of the Fifth Week of Lent give way to those of the solemnity. The Gloria and the Creed are said; the Gospel acclamation is sung without Alleluia, as throughout Lent. Because today is a solemnity, the Friday obligation of abstinence does not bind this year (Code of Canon Law, can. 1251); many still choose another act of penance or charity. When 19 March falls in Holy Week the solemnity is moved, but in 2027 it is kept on its own day. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-03-19.verse: When Joseph awoke from sleep, he did as the angel of the Lord commanded him; he took her as his wife
theo: In the middle of the last fortnight of Lent the Church puts on white for the man to whom God entrusted his greatest treasures. St Joseph never speaks a single word in the Gospels, yet everything depends on his listening. The first reading takes us back a thousand years before him. King David wants to build a house for God, and God answers through the prophet Nathan that he will build a house for David instead: “I will raise up your offspring after you… and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever. I will be a father to him, and he shall be a son to me… Your house and your kingdom shall be made sure forever before me.” By the time of Jesus the royal line of David had fallen into obscurity; its heir was a carpenter in Nazareth. Matthew's genealogy ends with “Jacob the father of Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom Jesus was born, who is called the Messiah.” Notice the care: Joseph is not called the father who begot Jesus, but the husband of Mary. Yet through Joseph's legal fatherhood, through his giving the child a name, Jesus is grafted into the house of David. The angel greets him as “Joseph, son of David.” God's promise to David passes through the hands of this silent, faithful man.

Matthew tells us what Joseph faced. Mary, already betrothed to him, “was found to be with child from the Holy Spirit.” Joseph, “being a righteous man and unwilling to expose her to public disgrace, planned to dismiss her quietly.” His righteousness is not cold law; it is mercy and reverence before a mystery he does not yet understand. Then the angel speaks in a dream: “do not be afraid to take Mary as your wife, for the child conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit. She will bear a son, and you are to name him Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins.” And Joseph's whole answer is action: “When Joseph awoke from sleep, he did as the angel of the Lord commanded him; he took her as his wife.” St Paul's words about Abraham in the second reading fit Joseph perfectly: “Hoping against hope, he believed,” and his faith “was reckoned to him as righteousness.” Where the alternative Gospel is read, Luke shows Joseph and Mary searching three days for the twelve-year-old Jesus and finding him in the Temple. Mary says, “your father and I have been searching for you in great anxiety,” and Jesus answers, “Did you not know that I must be in my Father's house?” Joseph accepts that the boy he raises belongs first to another Father, and still Jesus “went down with them and came to Nazareth, and was obedient to them.” The Son of God learned to work, to pray the psalms and to keep the law at Joseph's side.

The Church has slowly come to see how great this hidden man is. Blessed Pius IX declared St Joseph Patron of the Universal Church in 1870; Leo XIII wrote about him in Quamquam Pluries (1889); St John Paul II called him the Guardian of the Redeemer (Redemptoris Custos, 1989); and Pope Francis, in Patris Corde (2020), described him as a beloved, tender, obedient, accepting, creatively courageous and working father, a father in the shadow. Joseph is patron of families, of workers, of fathers, of those who must make hard decisions in the night, and of a happy death, since he died, as tradition holds, in the arms of Jesus and Mary. In many parishes in Kerala this day brings a festive meal for the poor and for all who come, remembering the man who fed the Holy Family with the work of his hands. Even in Lent, today is a day of joy. We ask St Joseph to guard the Church as he guarded the child and his mother, and to teach us his way: to listen, to rise, and to do what God asks without many words.
conn: Joseph's genealogy in Matthew runs from Abraham through David. By naming the child, Joseph gives Jesus his legal place in David's line (Matthew 1:20–21; Luke 1:27).

In Jewish custom betrothal was already a binding marriage; the bride lived in her father's house until the husband took her to his home. That is why Matthew calls Joseph her husband before they lived together.
In Matthew, God speaks to Joseph four times in dreams: to take Mary (1:20), to flee to Egypt (2:13), to return (2:19–20) and to settle in Galilee (2:22). Each time he obeys at once.
The Greek word dikaios describes one who lives faithfully by God's law. Joseph's righteousness shows itself in mercy and in obedience to God's new word.
Matthew 13:55 calls Jesus the carpenter's son; the Greek tekton means a builder or craftsman in wood and stone. Joseph is honoured on 1 May as St Joseph the Worker.
As a solemnity, today has the Gloria and the Creed, and the Friday abstinence does not bind (can. 1251). In some years 19 March falls in Holy Week and the solemnity is moved.
altar: Joseph held in his arms the Body of the Lord that we receive at the altar. St Bernard compares him to the patriarch Joseph, who stored bread for a starving world: this Joseph guarded the living Bread come down from heaven.

St Joseph is named in the Eucharistic Prayers, after the Virgin Mary, since Pope Francis added his name in 2013 to the Second, Third and Fourth Eucharistic Prayers. The silent guardian stands beside us at every Mass.
outline: Ask: who are the quiet people who have protected and provided for you without many words?
God's promise passes through a carpenter.
Mercy, reverence and a dilemma in the night.
The faith of Abraham in the heart of Joseph.
He went down with them and was obedient to them.
A carpenter's hands holding a sleeping child.
“He did as the angel of the Lord commanded him.”
live: Name one thing God has been asking of you, and do it today without delay.
Like Joseph, take care of someone vulnerable in your family or neighbourhood this week.
Offer your work today to God through St Joseph, and do it well and honestly.
Pray for the dying today, and ask St Joseph, patron of a happy death, to be with them.
fathers: The patriarch Joseph stored up grain, not for himself but for all the people; this Joseph received the living Bread from heaven and kept it for himself and for the whole world. He is the faithful and prudent servant whom the Lord set over his household.

Whenever God chooses someone for a special grace or a high office, he gives that person all the gifts needed for it. So it was with Joseph, chosen by the eternal Father as the faithful foster-father and guardian of his chief treasures, his Son and his Son's mother.

I took the glorious St Joseph as my advocate and patron, and I do not remember ever asking anything of him that he failed to grant. I would like to persuade everyone to be devoted to this glorious saint.
magis: The angel's message to Joseph; the virginal conception of Jesus by the Holy Spirit.
The hidden life at Nazareth and the finding in the Temple.
St Joseph, patron of a happy death.
Joseph, Guardian of the Redeemer, in the life of Christ and of the Church.
Joseph, a beloved, tender, obedient, accepting, creatively courageous and working father, a father in the shadow.
saints: Of the house of David, a craftsman of Nazareth, husband of the Virgin Mary and legal father of Jesus. He protected Mary and the child, fled with them to Egypt, raised Jesus at Nazareth and, according to tradition, died before Jesus' public ministry. Patron of the Universal Church (1870).
15–20 Mar: Lenten weekdays of the fifth week; 17 Mar: St Patrick; 18 Mar: St Cyril of Jerusalem (commemorations). 21 Mar: Palm Sunday of the Passion of the Lord; Holy Week begins.
2027-03-19.prayer: Grant, we pray, almighty God, that by Saint Joseph's intercession your Church may constantly watch over the unfolding of the mysteries of human salvation, whose beginnings you entrusted to his faithful care. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen. Let us also pray: St Joseph, son of David, husband of Mary and guardian of the Redeemer, protect our families, our workers and our Church. Teach us to listen to God in the night, to rise and obey, and to love Jesus and Mary as you loved them. Be with us and with all the dying at the hour of our death. Amen.

quick: God's promise to David was fulfilled through Joseph, who gave Jesus his name and his place in David's line.
Joseph, a righteous man, believed the angel and took Mary as his wife.
St Joseph is Patron of the Universal Church, of families, workers and a happy death.
2027-03-19.action: Do at once one thing you know God is asking of you, as Joseph did.
2027-03-19.question: When God's plan upsets mine, do I respond like Joseph, with trust and action?
catechism: The angel announces to Joseph the birth of the Messiah.
The hidden life of Jesus at Nazareth with Mary and Joseph.
St Joseph, patron of a happy death.
kidsaint: Joseph was a carpenter in Nazareth. God asked him to look after Mary and baby Jesus. He listened to God's angel in his dreams and always obeyed straight away. He kept Jesus safe, taught him to work and loved him like the best of fathers. Lesson: listen to God and do what he asks, quickly and with love.
2027-03-19.special: Solemnity of St Joseph, Spouse of the Blessed Virgin Mary. White vestments, Gloria and Creed; Friday abstinence does not bind on this solemnity.
term: The highest rank of celebration in the Roman calendar. A solemnity has the Gloria and the Creed and its own readings, and when it falls on a Friday the obligation of abstinence does not apply (can. 1251).

family.explain: Joseph was going to marry Mary. When he learned she was going to have a baby, he was worried. But an angel told him in a dream: do not be afraid, the baby is from the Holy Spirit, call him Jesus. Joseph woke up and did just what the angel said. He became the protector of Jesus and Mary.
family.intention: We pray for all fathers, for workers who have no work, and for the dying.
family.ask: Ask: “How does our father, or someone like a father to us, protect and care for our family? Let us thank him today.”

illus: In a parish near Kottayam, the St Joseph's day meal draws hundreds: day labourers, old people living alone, children, migrant workers who speak little Malayalam. A retired carpenter has served rice there for forty years. Asked why, he said: St Joseph fed Jesus with the work of his hands. I am only a carpenter too. Once a year I can feed Jesus in these people.

pm.open: St Joseph, son of David and guardian of the Redeemer, pray for us, and teach us to listen and obey. Amen.
share: Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid (Matthew 1:20). What fear keeps me from doing God's will?
He did as the angel of the Lord commanded him (Matthew 1:24). How quickly do I obey when God speaks?
Hoping against hope, he believed (Romans 4:18). Where do I need hope against hope?
pm.resp: His dynasty shall last for ever.
interc: For the whole Church, entrusted to the protection of St Joseph.
For fathers, that they may be loving, faithful and present like Joseph.
For workers, the unemployed and migrants, that they may find dignified work.
For families facing hard decisions, that they may hear God's voice.
For the dying, that St Joseph may obtain for them a holy death in the arms of Jesus and Mary.
pm.close: Father, you entrusted the beginnings of our salvation to the faithful care of St Joseph. Through his prayers, protect your Church. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, in the middle of Lent we put on white to honour St Joseph. In the whole Gospel he does not say a single word. Yet God entrusted to him his two greatest treasures: his only Son and the Virgin Mary.

God promised David: I will raise up your offspring after you… and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever (2 Samuel 7:12–13). A thousand years later the heir of David is a carpenter in Nazareth. Through Joseph, who gives the child his name, Jesus becomes son of David. God keeps his promises through humble people.

Joseph's world is turned upside down: Mary is with child. Being a righteous man and unwilling to expose her to public disgrace, he planned to dismiss her quietly (Matthew 1:19). His goodness is full of mercy. But God has a bigger plan, and an angel tells him in a dream: Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary as your wife (Matthew 1:20).

Then come the most beautiful words about him: when Joseph awoke from sleep, he did as the angel of the Lord commanded him (Matthew 1:24). No argument, no delay. Like Abraham, hoping against hope, he believed (Romans 4:18). Joseph teaches us that faith is not many words, but quiet obedience.

At Nazareth Jesus went down with Mary and Joseph and was obedient to them. The Son of God learned to work with wood, to pray and to keep the law at Joseph's side. Every father, every worker, every person who cares for others in silence can look to Joseph and find his own vocation honoured.

Let us entrust ourselves today to St Joseph: our families, our work, our Church and our last hour. May he teach us to listen to God in the night, to rise, and to do what God asks. St Joseph, pray for us. Amen.
kids: Children, St Joseph was a carpenter. He took care of Jesus and Mary, kept them safe, worked hard to give them food, and taught Jesus how to make things with wood.
When God spoke to Joseph, he obeyed straight away. Today, when Mummy or Daddy asks you to do something good, do it straight away, like St Joseph!

intro: In Egypt, when the people were hungry, Pharaoh said: “Go to Joseph.” The Church says the same to us about the Joseph of Nazareth, guardian of Jesus and of his Church.

sub: The patriarch Joseph fed a starving land.
The new Joseph guards the Bread of Life.
points.apply: Each day pray one Our Father and one Hail Mary in honour of St Joseph, for your family's needs.
Pray to St Joseph for refugees and for families in danger.

sub: He guards the Body as he guarded the Child.
points.apply: Each night, ask St Joseph for the grace of a holy death.

concl: As Joseph guarded Jesus and Mary, he guards the Church and every Christian family.
Go to Joseph, and he will lead you to Jesus.
opts.resolve: This week I will entrust my family, my work and my last hour to St Joseph.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, long ago in Egypt there was a great famine. When the people cried to Pharaoh for bread, he said: go to Joseph; what he says to you, do (Genesis 41:55). That Joseph had stored grain and saved a whole nation. The Church has always seen in him a figure of our St Joseph, who guarded the true Bread from heaven, Jesus.

Joseph of Nazareth was not only obedient; he was a protector. When Herod sought to kill the child, an angel said to him: get up, take the child and his mother, and flee to Egypt, and remain there until I tell you (Matthew 2:13). Then Joseph got up, took the child and his mother by night, and went to Egypt (Matthew 2:14). He became a refugee to keep Jesus alive. Pope Francis spoke of Joseph's creative courage: in a foreign land, with no work and no home, he found a way.

In 1870 Blessed Pius IX declared St Joseph Patron of the Universal Church. The reason is simple. Christ is the head of the body, the church (Colossians 1:18). The man who guarded the body of Jesus at Nazareth now guards his body, the Church, throughout the world. Unless the LORD builds the house, those who build it labor in vain (Psalm 127:1). Joseph built a house where God was at home.

Tradition also calls him the patron of a holy death, because he died, we believe, in the arms of Jesus and Mary. What better way could anyone die? So Christians have always prayed to him for their last hour, that they too may die with Jesus and Mary beside them.

So let us go to Joseph. Let us bring him our families, our work, our worries about money and housing, and our last hour. He who protected Jesus in the night will protect us. And he will lead us, as he led the Child, to the altar of God at every Mass. St Joseph, pray for us. Amen.

intro: The alternative Gospel today shows Joseph at a frightening moment: the boy Jesus is lost for three days. We see a father who searches, who does not understand, and who keeps going.

sub: Joseph leads the household in worship.
points.apply: Bring your whole family to Sunday Mass together this week.

sub: A day's journey before they notice.

concl: Joseph is a model for every father who searches, suffers and keeps faith.
Even when he did not understand, he kept doing his duty with love.
opts.resolve: This week I will pray for parents who are searching for their children, and thank God for my own father.
homily: Dear friends, the alternative Gospel for today takes us to Jerusalem. Every year Joseph and Mary went to Jerusalem for the festival of the Passover (Luke 2:41). The law asked men to go up to the Lord three times a year (Deuteronomy 16:16). Joseph did not leave religion to his wife. He led his household in worship. A father who prays and goes to church teaches more than a hundred sermons.

Then the terrible moment. On the way home they discover that Jesus is not with them. Assuming that he was in the group of travelers, they went a day's journey (Luke 2:44). Then three days of searching through crowded streets. Every parent here knows that fear. When they find him in the temple, Mary says: Child, why have you treated us like this? Look, your father and I have been searching for you in great anxiety (Luke 2:48).

Notice: your father and I. Mary speaks of Joseph as the father of Jesus. He was not his father by blood, but he was truly his father by love, by law and by care. And he suffered as a father suffers. The bride in the Song of Songs says: I will seek him whom my soul loves (Song of Songs 3:2). Joseph and Mary sought Jesus with that love.

Jesus answers: did you not know that I must be in my Father's house? (Luke 2:49). They did not understand. Joseph had to accept that this child belonged first to God. And yet: then he went down with them and came to Nazareth, and was obedient to them (Luke 2:51). The Son of God obeyed Joseph. Joseph kept his place with humility, neither possessive nor absent.

Today let us pray for all fathers, and for parents who are searching for children who have left home or left the faith. Do not give up. Joseph searched three days and found Jesus in the house of God. Let us bring our children to the Mass, and let us ask St Joseph to help every father to lead, to protect and to love. Amen.

intro: Theme: “When Joseph awoke from sleep, he did as the angel of the Lord commanded him.”
The son of David, the righteous man, the faith of Abraham, and the guardian of the Redeemer.

q: Your house and your kingdom shall be made sure forever before me; your throne shall be established forever.

But just when he had resolved to do this, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream and said, “Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary as your wife, for the child conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit.
points.apply: Thank God this week for the people through whom his promises reached you: parents, godparents, teachers.

q: The righteous walk in integrity, happy are the children who follow them!
Her husband Joseph, being a righteous man and unwilling to expose her to public disgrace, planned to dismiss her quietly.

concl: God fulfilled his promise to David through the silent faithfulness of Joseph.
